inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: thick fog is expected in western regions of the UAE. Visibility may drop to zero at times from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Drive with extreme caution. More: https://alerts.example.ae
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions tonight until 10:00 Wednesday
fields.instruction: If you drive, slow down, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow the modified speed limits. Follow all traffic safety guidelines.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded on that basis.
No specific roads, towns or emirates are named, because the NCM statement only says 'several western regions of the UAE'.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and certainty to Likely because NCM describes 'potential' fog, but says visibility may fall to zero. Please confirm whether you want Severe instead. Also check that the operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' matches NCM's 'several western regions'.

objections.fix: Reword to match the bulletin, e.g. 'Fog may form and visibility is expected to deteriorate in several western regions, and may drop to zero at times.' Set certainty to Possible, or keep Likely only if the NCM statement supports a probability above 50%. Otherwise leave the decision to a person.
objections.issue: The description states 'thick fog is expected', and certainty is set to Likely. The bulletin says only 'potential fog formation' with reduced visibility 'expected to deteriorate'. Thick fog is mentioned only for 'areas experiencing thick fog', as a driving-advice condition. The alert therefore overstates certainty and the extent of thick fog.

payload.summary: The alert matches the bulletin on hazard, times and area. Two points differ from it. The description says 'thick fog is expected', but the bulletin only speaks of 'potential fog formation', so the alert is more certain than the bulletin. The alert also adds a Moderate severity and a Likely certainty that the bulletin does not give.

no_basis.concern: The register entry is a demo stand-in for the real issuer, so it cannot be confirmed that the real NCEMA or other UAE authority has authorised this sender. The WMO register also leaves the authorization basis and alerting area blank.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE issuer register entries or authorization basis confirming the sender and its alerting area

payload.summary: Within my mandate nothing is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with wildcard areas and categories. The alert area (Western region demo zone, DEMO-ZONE/AUH-WEST) matches the area drawn for event uae-fog-2026-02-17. Status Actual with msgType Alert fits a real event on a live console. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach, and no earlier alerts, so no correction or reference is needed.

objections.fix: Reorder both language texts so that the hazard and the action come first, e.g. 'Fog warning: drive with extreme caution. Visibility may drop to zero in western UAE...'. In Arabic, put 'قُد بحذر شديد' right after the short hazard phrase, within the first 41 characters. Then place the timing and the link afterwards.
objections.issue: The first page does not carry the action. In English the first ~93 characters cover only the hazard and place. 'Drive with extreme caution' only appears in page 3. In Arabic (41 characters per page) page 1 holds only the start of the hazard sentence and the action 'قُد بحذر شديد' falls on page 6. A handset user who sees only page 1 gets no instruction.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. The page counts of 3 (GSM-7) and 6 (UCS-2) are under the 15-page maximum, and the encodings are consistent with the text. However, the action instruction sits on the last page in both languages, so the first page carries the hazard but not the action.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic was produced by machine translation with no recorded human review. The text is accurate on comparison, but a named person who reads Arabic must still sign off.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE or TDRA clause requiring human review of machine-translated Arabic in emergency alerts; only FCC (US) clauses speak to this, and none from the UAE

The Arabic was machine translated, so a named Arabic reader must still approve it before sending.
